handbookNote: Rhode Island Real Estate Broker license exam. Part of the 2026-09-03 R26 population-tier broker buildout (population order: UT > NV > IA > AR > KS > MS > ID > NE > WV > HI > NH > MT > RI > DE > SD > ND > AK > VT > WY). Exam vendor: Pearson VUE, under contract with the RI Dept. of Business Regulation (DBR) (Candidate Handbook #094000, January 2026). National/General Part: 80 scored items + 5 unscored pretest, 2.5 hours. Rhode Island State Part: 60 scored items (vs. 50 for Salesperson) + 10 unscored pretest, 1.5 hours. The two parts are separately scheduled/scored/paid exams, not one combined sitting (140 scored items / 4.0 hours total testing time if summed). Passing score is a SCALED score of 70 (0-100 scale, NOT a raw percent-correct threshold), National and State scored/passed INDEPENDENTLY (retake only the failed part, results valid 1 year). track_registry models this as exam_question_count=140, exam_duration_sec=14400, pass_percent=70, min_correct=98 (round(140*0.70)), same scaled-score convention as UT/NV/KS/ID/NE/WV/WY/AK/DE/MT in this campaign. NATIONAL/GENERAL PORTION (80 items, 8 sections) reuses the exact same real Pearson VUE national item bank as Utah/Nevada/Kansas/Idaho/Nebraska/West Virginia/Montana -- Rhode Island's own Broker outline weights are IDENTICAL (10/8/10/15/12/9/8/8 across the same 8 sections). RHODE ISLAND STATE PORTION (60 items, real Broker item counts): Duties and Obligations Under Licensing Law (2, DBR's real statutory powers under RIGL 5-20.5-3/4/6 and the RI Real Estate Commission's real advisory role within DBR -- 9 members, 3 brokers/4 public/2 ex-officio, 5-yr terms), Licensing Requirements (6, real broker eligibility -- 2 years full-time salesperson experience + 90 broker-specific classroom hours (distinct from/on top of the 45 salesperson hours), 24-hr CE incl. 9-hr CORE/3-hr fair-housing minimums, RIGL 5-20.5-4/5-20.5-6), Statutory Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees (22, largest single section -- real RIGL 5-20.5-14's 37-subsection prohibited-conduct list, the distinctive RIGL 5-20.5-21 rule limiting commission-suit standing to licensed brokers, and Rhode Island's real, narrow unauthorized-practice-of-law exemption letting licensees prepare purchase-and-sale agreements/leases they negotiated but never deeds), Additional Topics (18, 11 distinct RI statutes/regulations incl. RIGL 34-37 Fair Housing, RIGL 34-18 Landlord-Tenant, RIGL 44-30-71.3 non-resident seller withholding, 216-RICR-50-15-3 Lead Disclosure, the Rhode Island Sales Disclosure Act (RIGL 5-20.8), the Rhode Island Condominium Act (RIGL 34-36.1 -- corrected from the outline's stale/miscited '34-36-1.1'), and RIGL 5-20.6's real 5-relationship-type agency framework), and Broker Only (12, no Salesperson equivalent -- RIGL 5-20.5-27's real license-required-for-ownership rule, escrow-account rules (180-day disputed-funds-to-treasurer deadline, 10-day release payout), 3-year recordkeeping retention, and the real investigation/hearing/appeal/sanction process incl. two distinct statutory penalty mechanisms, RIGL 5-20.5-14's $2,000 admin-penalty cap and RIGL 5-20.5-17's separate tiered fine schedule up to $5,000 for corporate repeat offenses). Governing law: RIGL Title 5, Chapter 20.5 (Real Estate Brokers and Salespersons) and 230-RICR-30-20-2 (RI Code of Regulations). Real Estate Recovery Account CONFIRMED PRESENT under RIGL 5-20.5-5 -- $50,000 per-licensee cap, $200,000 replenishment trigger, funded in part by a real $25 broker-application fee (a genuinely distinct funding/consumer-protection model from Montana's repealed fund/E&O-insurance-only approach and New Hampshire's surety-bond model, both handled elsewhere in this campaign). This bank was drafted across 5 new state-topic drafting passes (the 8 national files were reused, not redrafted). Answers were deterministically rotated into final A/B/C/D position via scripts/tracks/rotate_broker_answers.js.
